title: Grand Societal Challenges and Responsible Innovation
summary: Grand societal challenges (GSCs) represent complex, multi‐level, multi‐dimensional problems that require concerted efforts by various actors – public, private, and non‐profit – to be successfully addressed. Businesses – alone or in conjunction with governmental and non‐profit organizations – are relevant actors in this regard, as they represent a source of innovation. Responsible innovation (RI) is a framework that allows for the governance and evaluation of innovations with regard to their potential harmful consequences and positive contributions to societal challenges. Moreover, it stipulates that this evaluation process should be facilitated by appropriate governance structures at various levels. The aim of this article is to expand theorizing on GSCs and RI and to encourage research that explores their links. We outline pertinent characteristics of GSCs that make current conceptualizations of corporate social responsibility and social innovation limited in addressing GSCs. We explicate the reflexive and participative capacities of RI governance as a complementary and promising way forward. Finally, we introduce the contributions to this Special Issue as illustrations of relevant theoretical and empirical groundwork around GSCs and RI, and outline the agenda for future research.

title: Caracterización de la gobernanza interna en unidades de producción de ganado bovino de doble propósito en el estado de Veracruz, México
summary: El análisis del perfil de gobernanza constituye un elemento clave para comprender cómo se estructuran y gestionan las explotaciones agropecuarias, ya que permite identificar los mecanismos de toma de decisiones, la organización del trabajo, la participación familiar y el acceso a recursos que influyen en su desempeño y sostenibilidad. El objetivo de este estudio fue caracterizar el perfil de gobernanza en una muestra de 132 unidades de producción (UP) elegidas al azar del Estado de Veracruz, con vistas al diseño de un programa de mejora en la gestión. Se analizaron 41 variables (19 cuantitativas y 22 cualitativas), relacionadas con la organización interna, toma de decisiones, participación, condiciones laborales, reinversión, acceso a capacitaciones y vínculos institucionales. Se realizó un análisis descriptivo, comparativo y de correlación para identificar asociaciones entre los principales elementos de gobernanza y las características socio-productivas de las UP. Aunque los resultados obtenidos evidenciaron una alta variabilidad en el patrón de gobernanza, sólo se detectaron diferencias significativas asociadas al binomio género y la experiencia profesional en calidad de vida, mano de obra familiar, diversificación en la remuneración y origen geográfico de los trabajadores, fuente principal de ingresos, y tipo de tenencia y régimen legal de la tierra. El análisis de correlación mostró asociación entre elementos claves de la gobernanza, como la opinión de los trabajadores en la toma de decisiones y el grado de diversificación de ingresos en la explotación (0.35). De manera general, las UP presentaron debilidades en su estructura organizacional, acceso limitado a financiamiento y asistencia técnica. No obstante, se identificó interés por parte de los productores en acceder a modelos que permitan incrementar los ingresos y fortalecer la sostenibilidad. Esta información resultó relevante para el diseño de estrategias orientadas al fortalecimiento de la gobernanza y la sostenibilidad de las UP estudiadas bajo el enfoque ESG.

title: STRATEGY FOR ENSURING ORGANIZATIONAL RESILIENCE: EVOLUTION FROM JUST-IN-TIME TO JUST-IN-CASE
summary: The study is devoted to the systemic transformation of conceptual foundations of strategic management and the assurance of organizational resilience of business entities under conditions of extreme macroenvironmental turbulence, severe economic shocks, and ongoing military-political instability. The paper comprehensively highlights the evolutionary transition from the traditional lean production concept Just-in-Time (JIT), focused on total minimization of inventory, operational cost reduction, and maximum efficiency, to the preventive Just-in-Case (JIC) model, which prioritizes the formation of strategic buffers, operational safety, and long-term business continuity. It is proven that excessive optimization within the JIT paradigm creates critical vulnerability in global supply chains during unexpected force majeure circumstances. The concept of "dynamic buffering" is substantiated as an economically sound alternative to chaotic resource accumulation, based on ABC risk analysis and optimization of the Cost of Resilience. Strategic adaptation tools are analyzed, including multi-sourcing supplier diversification, nearshoring, friendshoring, as well as the transition to "glocalization" and ecosystem partnership models with deep inter-organizational process integration. Special attention is paid to digital transformation as a fundamental factor of resilience, specifically the implementation of artificial intelligence, end-to-end visibility systems, digital twins for proactive scenario crisis modeling, and ensuring comprehensive cybersecurity and information continuity of IT infrastructure. The crucial role of strategic leadership, predictive risk management, scenario planning, Agile methodologies implementation, and corporate culture transformation from "zero waste" to perceiving "justified redundancy" as strategic insurance is identified. New performance evaluation metrics for crisis conditions are proposed, including Time to Survive (TTS) and Time to Recover (TTR), alongside examining the specifics of building "collaborative resilience" in the small and medium enterprise sector through partner networks and resource sharing.

title: The Fiduciary Duty of Loyalty
summary: The fiduciary duty of loyalty constitutes one of the fundamental principles of contemporary corporate law and serves as the primary legal mechanism for identifying and regulating directors' conflicts of interest. Despite its central role in English-American corporate law, the conceptual structure of fiduciary duty of loyalty has undergone significant refinement following the publication of the American Law Institute's Restatement of the Law, 2022, Corporate Governance. This Article examines the contemporary understanding of the duty of loyalty and evaluates its significance for the interpretation of Georgian corporate law. The research employs doctrinal legal analysis supported by content analysis, comparative and historical methodologies. It analyses legislation and judicial decisions relating to directors' fiduciary duties, conflicts of interest, the Business Judgment Rule and corporate governance in the United States, Continental Europe and in the Georgian legal system. The Article argues that the Restatement does not create a new fiduciary obligation but rather systematizes existing judicial doctrine into a coherent analytical framework centered upon the duty of loyalty. It further establishes that good faith forms an integral subsidiary element of the duty of loyalty and that the Business Judgment Rule should be understood primarily as a standard of judicial review rather than merely as a component of the duty of care. Comparative analysis also reveals that Georgian corporate law regulates numerous features of fiduciary loyalty, although these features remain fragmented across different statutory provisions. The American Law Institute's Restatement of the Law, 2022, provides a persuasive comparative framework for the systematization of fiduciary duties and contributes to greater doctrinal coherence, legal certainty and consistency in judicial decision-making processes.

title: IMPROVING THE ACCOUNTING AND AUDIT OF TAX OBLIGATIONS
summary: The article examines the theoretical and methodological issues of recognising, measuring, and auditing tax liabilities. It proposes a three-layer conceptual framework integrating financial accounting, tax reporting, and internal controls, a multi-criteria tax risk index, and a risk-based audit procedure.

title: Diversification Strategies, Corporate Governance Disclosure and Financial Performance of Agricultural Firms Listed at the Nairobi Securities Exchange, Kenya
summary: Agricultural firms listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE) have recorded uneven financial performance, and evidence on whether diversification improves performance remains inconsistent. Little is known about whether corporate governance disclosure (CGD) lies on the path between diversification and performance. This study examined the association of horizontal, concentric, and conglomerate diversification with financial performance, measured by Return on Assets (ROA), and whether CGD mediated each association. The study was anchored on the Resource-Based View, supported by agency and signalling perspectives. An explanatory, longitudinal design was used with secondary data from the audited annual reports of the six agricultural firms listed at the NSE, studied as a census over 2019 to 2024 (36 firm-years). CGD was scored with a 50-item index adapted from Varshney et al. (2015) and Shrivastav and Kalsie (2017). Data were analysed using hierarchical regression, the Sobel test and bootstrap confidence intervals, followed by sensitivity checks. None of the three diversification types was associated with ROA at the 5% level, but adding CGD raised R² by .140 (B = 0.176, p = .022). CGD showed a statistically supported indirect association for horizontal diversification (indirect effect = 0.677, 95% CI [0.260, 1.124]) and concentric diversification (0.229, 95% CI [0.088, 0.383]), but not for conglomerate diversification. The horizontal result depended on Kakuzi Plc, the CGD coefficient was not significant under firm fixed effects, and all findings were associations in a six-firm census and not causal effects. The study recommends that boards strengthen governance disclosure and monitoring alongside diversification decisions, and that the Capital Markets Authority and the NSE issue guidance on the consistency of governance and segment reporting.

title: Towards smarter universities: how Quality 4.0 and digital knowledge management drive operational performance in higher education institutions
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine the impact of Quality 4.0 (Q4.0) dimensions on operational performance improvement (OPI) in higher education institutions, with a particular focus on the mediating role of digital knowledge management (DKM). The research responds to the growing need for digital transformation in the education sector by exploring how Q4.0 technologies can enhance operational efficiency, academic quality, and institutional sustainability. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was adopted, using data collected from 1,154 faculty members across three major universities in a developing country. The study employed Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) to assess the direct and indirect relationships among five Q4.0 dimensions-digital transformation (DT), analytics and big data (ABD), communication and collaboration (CC), innovation and sustainability (IS), and adaptability to change (CA)-DKM, and OPI. Findings The results reveal that all five Q4.0 dimensions have significant positive effects on operational performance. Additionally, DKM exerts both a direct influence on OPI and a mediating effect between Q4.0 practices and institutional performance outcomes. The study confirms that effective DKM enhances the benefits of digital initiatives by facilitating knowledge sharing, data-driven decision-making, and operational agility within higher education institutions. Originality/value This research contributes to the literature by introducing an integrated conceptual model that bridges Q4.0 and DKM within the context of higher education – a setting underexplored in existing research. It provides empirical evidence from a developing country context and highlights the strategic role of DKM in maximising the impact of digital transformation initiatives. The study offers practical insights for academic leaders and policymakers aiming to improve institutional performance through targeted digital strategies.

title: Between pixels and emotions: semiotic-NLP deconstruction of cultural heritage’s social media image
summary: Abstract This study investigates how digital transformation reshapes the representation and perception of cultural heritage within contemporary tourism by analysing social media narratives of three key urban heritage attractions in Ankara: Hamamönü, Ankara Castle, and the Museum of Anatolian Civilizations. Using a mixed-methods approach, the research integrates visual semiotic analysis—examining colour schemes, compositional patterns, and symbolic codes—with NLP-based sentiment classification of user-generated content from X, Instagram, and Facebook. Findings show Hamamönü is primarily represented through traditional architecture (41%) and gastronomy-focused experiences (34%), emphasizing its cultural and experiential identity. Ankara Castle highlights archaeological heritage (38%) and the urban landscape (29%), underscoring historical and spatial dimensions. The Museum of Anatolian Civilizations is associated with educational value (45%) and interactive exhibition practices (27%), reflecting its strong role in digitally mediated museum experiences. Sentiment analysis indicates polarization: museum-related posts are overwhelmingly positive (82%), whereas critiques focus on Castle infrastructure (28%) and visitor management issues (19%). Overall, the study provides a data-driven framework demonstrating how social media analytics can guide evidence-based strategies for digital transformation, effective promotion, and sustainable communication of cultural heritage sites.

title: Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for Sustainable Development and Business Transformation: A Conceptual Study
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly positioned at the intersection of business transformation and sustainable development. Its capacity to identify patterns in large datasets, forecast demand and risk, automate routine processes, support product innovation, and improve resource allocation creates opportunities to enhance organizational performance while addressing environmental and social priorities. Yet these outcomes are not automatic: AI can reproduce bias, intensify surveillance, displace or transform work, widen digital inequalities, and consume substantial energy and material resources. This conceptual study synthesizes the supplied literature review on AI-enabled sustainability, digital transformation, innovation, governance, and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It develops an integrated framework in which AI capabilities influence sustainable business transformation through three complementary mechanisms: operational and resource optimization, innovation capability, and data-driven decision-making. The proposed framework links AI adoption with economic, environmental, and social sustainability through digital infrastructure, workforce skills, organizational readiness, and collaboration. Responsible governance, fairness, accountability, and data protection ensure ethical implementation. AI-driven sustainability requires strategic alignment, organizational learning, and responsible practices to achieve measurable business transformation and sustainable outcomes. As a conceptual paper, it does not claim empirical validation; instead, it offers propositions and a research agenda for future survey, case-study, and structural-equation modelling research.

title: Regularized Government Accounting Supervision and Suppliers’ Cash Holdings: Evidence from Supply Chain Spillover Effects
summary: This article takes the reform pilot of strengthening accounting supervision carried out by the Ministry of Finance in selected provinces and municipalities at the end of 2020 as a quasi‑natural experiment, and adopts the difference‑in‑differences method to investigate the supply chain spillover effect of regularized government accounting supervision on the cash holding level of supplier firms. The study finds that when midstream firms are located in regions with the accounting supervision reform pilot, the cash holding level of their supplier firms decreases significantly. Mechanism tests show that regularized government accounting supervision functions mainly through two channels, namely reducing supply chain risks faced by suppliers and increasing the supply of trade credit. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the above effect is more pronounced among supplier firms that are state‑owned enterprises, have high customer concentration, and belong to high‑tech industries. This research expands the research boundary of the economic consequences of government accounting supervision, reveals the microeconomic effects of external regulatory institutions transmitted through supply chain relationships, and provides empirical evidence for improving China’s accounting supervision system and enhancing the financial resilience of supply chains.

title: Digital Constitutionalism and the Protection of Customary Law People’s Rights in Indonesia
summary: Digital revolution has altered the manner in which public authority is administered and how citizens engage with public services, partake in democratic activities, and assert their constitutional rights. This research examines the effects of digital transformation on the constitutional rights of customary law communities and delineates Indigenous Data Sovereignty within the Indonesian legal system. Contemporary studies on digital constitutionalism mostly emphasise individual rights, state power, and the governance of digital platforms, but Indigenous Data Sovereignty discourse specifically underscores collective management of Indigenous data. However, the relationship between these two fields remains insufficiently developed in Indonesia, particularly with communal data, indigenous wisdom, and cultural identity. This research employs a normative legal approach utilising statutory and conceptual frameworks. Primary and secondary legal texts were collected through library research and analysed qualitatively. The findings suggest that digital transformation improves cultural preservation, information availability, civic participation, and public service provision. Concurrently, it fosters unequal digital accessibility, administrative exclusion, diminishment of community control over collective data, and the unauthorised utilisation of indigenous knowledge without authorisation or fair benefit-sharing. Indonesia’s personal data protection framework primarily emphasises identifiable individuals and is deficient in explicit restrictions concerning communal data or collective detriment. This research contends that Indigenous Data Sovereignty should be founded on recognising communal data and customary law communities as collective rights-holders, employing consent based on traditional practices, guaranteeing community governance over data access and use, instituting benefit-sharing, performing collective impact assessments, ensuring institutional oversight, and delivering effective remedies.

title: OPTIMIZING THE WORKLOAD OF STATE ENFORCEMENT OFFICERS THROUGH DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES
summary: This article examines the growing workload of state enforcement officers, the increasing volume of enforcement documents and the challenges of using available human resources efficiently. It explores the use of digital technologies, automated data exchange, artificial intelligence and electronic monitoring in enforcement proceedings. The article proposes classifying enforcement actions according to complexity and automation potential, improving workload measurement and performance indicators, and reducing unnecessary manual operations. It also emphasizes the need to preserve qualitative performance standards, legal oversight and procedural safeguards throughout digital transformation.

title: Digital literacy, employment choices, and income disparities among migrant agricultural workers
summary: The investigation of the impact of digital literacy on the income growth and income disparities of migrant agricultural workers is of significant importance for advancing common prosperity among rural farmers. Based on China Family Panel Studies (CFPS) data, this study empirically tests the effect of digital literacy on migrant agricultural workers’ income and income disparities. The results show that improving digital literacy significantly increases the per capita income of migrant agricultural workers’ households and reduces the income gap. These findings remain valid after a series of robustness and endogeneity tests. Mechanism analysis suggests that digital literacy contributes to income growth and narrowing the income gap by influencing migrant agricultural workers’ formal employment, occupational choices, and industry transitions. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the income growth and gap reduction effects among migrant agricultural workers are more pronounced in the eastern region. However, it is noteworthy that, compared to the new generation and higher-educated migrant agricultural workers, the income growth and gap reduction effects are more pronounced among the older generation and lower-educated migrant agricultural workers. RIF unconditional quantile regression further finds that the income growth effect of digital literacy is strongest at the low-income end and weakens as income quantiles increase, while its effect on reducing income disparities is also concentrated at lower quantiles. Based on these findings, recommendations are proposed, such as improving the incentive mechanism for inclusive digital economy development and enhancing mechanisms for preventing income polarization among the rural migrant population.

title: Confucian ethical leadership as a moral strategist: driving corporate innovation through social-environmental and customer-oriented CSR
summary: Purpose This paper aims to address a gap in ethical leadership research by examining the culturally specific mechanism through which Confucian ethical leadership (CEL) influences corporate innovation – a domain where Western-dominated studies have underexplored the unique contributions of Eastern ethical traditions. Design/methodology/approach The study constructs a conceptual framework for CEL that bridges Western paradigms while highlighting its distinctiveness. It proposes a moderated mediation model in which social-environmental corporate social responsibility (CSR) mediates the CEL–innovation relationship and customer-oriented CSR moderates the direct effect of CEL on innovation. Data were collected from 151 case samples of Confucian-oriented firms in China using a case survey method, and PROCESS Model 5 with 5,000 bootstrap samples was employed for hypothesis testing. Findings The results demonstrate a significant positive effect of CEL on corporate innovation. Social-environmental CSR functions as a partial mediator, channeling CEL's influence into outcomes, while customer-oriented CSR acts as a positive moderator, strengthening the direct effect of CEL on innovation. This establishes a culturally distinct model for innovation that diverges from established Western frameworks. Originality/value This study proposes the concept of CEL as a “moral strategist,” embedding Confucian ethics into strategic decision-making to drive innovation through CSR. Unlike Western ethical leadership, which often emphasizes psychological processes or organizational climates, CEL fosters innovation through culturally rooted mechanisms centered on relational harmony and societal welfare. By contrasting these approaches, the study offers theoretical understanding of the ethical leadership-innovation nexus and contributes to cross-cultural ethical leadership research, offering insights for culturally adaptive innovation governance in global business contexts.

title: Governing the Energy Transition: Management Privatization as a Path to Security of Supply and Infrastructure Development
summary: Today, the OECD Guidelines for Corporate Governance of State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) are recognized worldwide as the benchmark for professionalizing the state’s role as an owner, ensuring that state-owned enterprises operate in an equally efficient and transparent manner to private enterprises. These international standards have become indispensable in the modern global economy, where the state remains a dominant actor in strategic sectors such as energy and infrastructure. The goal of this paper is to address the systematic issue of the „Implementation Gap“ in the energy sectors of transition economies, focusing specifically on the case of the Republic of North Macedonia. In these contexts, the imperative of a sustainable energy transition encompassing both security of supply and climate change mitigation is constantly challenged by the entrenched reality of state-led governance. Despite the normative commitment of SOEs in the Macedonian energy sector, such as JSC ESM and JSC MEPSO, toward these international benchmarks, the reality of political interference and institutional decoupling remains a significant barrier to progress. We have used the quantitative methods to investigate the quality of corporate governance through an instrumental multiple case study design, incorporating findings from 80 structured surveys and qualitative insights from 6 in-depth expert interviews. The findings have shown that there is a massive „Perception Gap“ of 1.70 points between the self-perception of internal board members and the observations of external stakeholders. The comparative aspect is covered by examining various types of governance structures, from the highly professionalized and centralized holding structures of Singapore (Temasek) and Slovenia (SDH) to the ongoing restructuring of the Serbian national utility, EPS – Elektroprivreda Srbije. Although the appointment of international experts for the EPS Supervisory Board, following IMF conditionalities, is a step towards OECD best practices, it is argued in the following research that North Macedonia needs to look beyond advisory-type oversight mechanisms. Instead, by synthesizing best practices from global and regional role models, a better solution for institutional insulation and operational efficiency is proposed. To break this cycle, the paper proposes a radical structural reform: a Mixed-Ownership Model with „Management Privatization.“ By inviting a highly credible international strategic partner to acquire a minority stake, the state can establish a robust „contractual shield“ against local political influence. The core rationale for inviting a strategic international partner through a mixed-ownership model is the urgent national need for both substantial capital injection and advanced technical expertise. This approach provides a direct benefit to the state by facilitating the construction of critical energy infrastructure, a sector where North Macedonia has faced a stagnation point with no significant large-scale projects realized in the past 30 years. By outsourcing management to a credible partner, the state secures the necessary investment and „know-how“ to finally modernize its aging assets and build the critical systems required for long-term energy independence

title: THE EFFECT OF THE BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS, INDEPENDENT COMMISSIONERS, AND GENDER ON ERM WITH FIRM SIZE AS A MODERATION
summary: This research examines the influence of board of commissioners size, independent commissioners, and gender diversity on Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) disclosure, with firm size as a moderating variable in basic materials sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2021–2024. Using a quantitative approach, this study employs secondary data collected from annual reports and purposive sampling, resulting in 293 observations. The data were analyzed using Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The findings indicate that board of commissioners size positively affects ERM disclosure, while independent commissioners negatively affect ERM disclosure. Meanwhile, gender diversity does not significantly influence ERM disclosure. The results further show that firm size weakens the relationship between board of commissioners size and ERM disclosure, strengthens the relationship between independent commissioners and ERM disclosure, and does not moderate the relationship between gender diversity and ERM disclosure. This study contributes to the corporate governance and risk management literature by highlighting the moderating role of firm size in the relationship between governance mechanisms and ERM disclosure within Indonesian basic materials firms. This context has received limited attention in prior studies.

title: THE EFFECT OF SUPPLY CHAIN AGILITY ON BUSINESS CONTINUITY OF FREIGHT FORWARDING COMPANIES UNDER GLOBAL SUPPLY CHAIN DISRUPTIONS
summary: Purpose - This study aims to analyze the influence of supply chain agility on business continuity in freight forwarding companies in dealing with uncertainty and supply chain disruption. Design/methodology/approach - The study used a quantitative, explanatory design. The study collected data through questionnaires from 55 freight forwarding companies and analyzed them using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Findings - The results show that supply chain agility has a positive, significant effect on business continuity, with a path coefficient of 0.953, a t-statistic of 35.171, and a p-value < 0.001. An R² value of 0.909 indicates that supply chain agility can explain 90.9% of business continuity variations. These findings confirm the importance of responsiveness to change, operational flexibility, resource reconfiguration, and information utilization in maintaining business continuity in freight forwarding companies. Originality/value - This research contributes by positioning business continuity as a direct outcome of supply chain agility in freight forwarding companies. This study expands the application of dynamic capabilities theory in the logistics services sector by showing that agility serves as a strategic capability for maintaining business functions during supply chain disruptions.

title: Corporate governance theory: a review of board effectiveness and financial performance of listed State owned Enterprises (SOEs) in Ghana
summary: This paper involves the empirical and theoretical literature on the systems of corporate governance. The overall objective of this research is to monitor, over a four-year period, the reported incidences of corporate governance practices at strategic listed state-owned enterprises (SOEs) in Ghana. Corporate governance practices for each SOEs were documented against the Ghana Stock Exchange (GSE) as well as the State Interests and Governance Authority (SIGA) best practice in governance for SOEs by reviewing annual financial reports and newspaper article citations over a four-year period.

title: CYBERSECURITY AS A PILLAR OF NATIONAL ECONOMIC SECURITY IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY: INTERNATIONAL EVIDENCE AND THE CASE OF UZBEKISTAN
summary: As economies digitalise, cyber incidents increasingly threaten output, financial stability and public trust, turning cybersecurity into a core component of national economic security. This article examines how cyber risk transmits into macroeconomic vulnerability and assesses Uzbekistan's policy response against international practice. Using document analysis, indicator comparison and three case studies (Estonia 2007, NotPetya 2017, Colonial Pipeline 2021), the study finds that economic losses arise mainly through concentration risk, supply-chain dependency and weak institutional capacity. Uzbekistan's ITU Global Cybersecurity Index score rose from 71.11 (2020) to 89.2 (2024), yet attack volumes and the human-capital gap remain significant. The article proposes six policy recommendations.

title: Information Technology Adoption and Business Model Innovation as Drivers of SME Competitiveness in Timor-Leste: A Conceptual Framework and Research Agenda
summary: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) play an important role in supporting economic diversification and employment in Timor-Leste. However, their competitiveness may be constrained by limited financial resources, digital capabilities, and market access. Although previous studies have examined digital technology adoption and business model innovation, these factors are often investigated separately or in contexts that may not fully reflect the conditions of SMEs in Timor-Leste. This study aims to develop a conceptual framework explaining how information technology adoption and business model innovation may contribute to SME competitiveness in Timor-Leste. A conceptual research approach was employed through a synthesis of relevant academic literature and institutional reports on digital transformation, business model innovation, and SME competitiveness. The synthesis indicates that information technology adoption may strengthen competitiveness through improved operational efficiency, broader market access, and better information management. Business model innovation may contribute by renewing how SMEs create, deliver, and capture value. The proposed framework positions these factors as two distinct but potentially complementary drivers of SME competitiveness and formulates two propositions for future empirical testing. The study’s novelty lies in integrating information technology adoption and business model innovation into a single conceptual framework specifically contextualized for SMEs in Timor-Leste. The framework provides a foundation for future empirical research and evidence-informed SME development policies.

title: HETEROGENEITY OF BOARD MEMBERSHIP AND INVESTORS' CONFIDENCE: AN EMPIRICAL APPRAISAL OF LISTED CONSUMER GOODS FIRMS IN NIGERIA
summary: The diversity of the board of directors of companies plays a crucial role in influencing investors’ confidence in such firms. However, investors’ confidence in Nigerian consumer goods firms seems to be influenced by factors other than diversity in board membership. Therefore this study was conducted to determine whether a relationship exists between the heterogeneity of board membership and investors’ confidence in Nigerian consumer goods firms. The independent variable of the study was the heterogeneity of board membership which was proxied by institutional board membership, board membership gender diversity, independent board membership, and board foreign membership; while the dependent variable was investors’ confidence which was proxied by price earnings ratio. The study population comprised of 17 consumer goods firms listed on the floor of the Nigerian Exchange Group within the period of 8 years, spanning 2018 to 2025, from which a sample of eight firms were selected. The study employed an ex post facto research design with data extracted from the selected firms’ published annual reports and accounts. The data obtained were analyzed with descriptive statistics and panel multiple regression model using E-view statistical packages version 10. The findings of the study revealed that institutional board membership (Coeff. = 0.208949, p-value = 0.0131), independent board membership (Coeff. = 2.864794, p-value = 0.0048), and foreign board membership (Coeff. = 1.864002, p-value = 0.0188) all have a significant positive relationship with the price earnings ratio, signifying that the presence of these categories board members influences the confidence of investors in the Nigerian consumer goods firms. However, board membership gender diversity (Coeff. = -0.259755, p-value = 0.9129) has no significant relationship with PER. It was concluded that the diversity of board membership influences investor’s confidence in Nigerian consumer goods firms. The recommendation included the need to include institutional investors in the board of Nigerian consumer goods firms

title: Ethical and legal dimensions of crowdsourcing professional services: a critical literature review
summary: Purpose The rapid shift from traditional face-to-face professional service delivery to digitally enabled crowdsourcing models, driven by automation and digitalisation, raises significant ethical and legal concerns. This study aims to critically examine the ethical and legal dimensions of professional crowdsourcing, focusing on its benefits, risks, governance challenges and implications for ethical integrity in the digital economy. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a qualitative critical literature review, methodologically guided by the SPAR-4-SLR and PRISMA methods. The chosen literature was then organised and synthesised using the Theory–Context–Characteristics–Methodology framework as the analytical framework. 56 of the 118 potentially pertinent articles that were found through a thorough search of Google Scholar and Scopus between 2000 and 2024 met the inclusion and quality requirements. The theoretcal underpinnings, research contexts, key ethical and legal aspects and methodological approaches of the retained studies were all synthesised. Findings Three findings emerged. First, professional crowdsourcing offers significant advantages, including wider access to expertise, lower transaction costs and faster service delivery, but it also raises systemic ethical and legal issues. Key concerns include fairness, accountability, algorithmic transparency, privacy, labour protections and regulatory uncertainty, which are often embedded in platform design rather than isolated incidents. Second, ethical management frameworks such as Stakeholder Theory, Social Contract Theory and Digital Ethics suggest that these risks stem from governance failures, power imbalances and opaque algorithmic processes, rather than from individual misconduct. Thirdly, insights from real-world cases on Amazon Mechanical Turk and Kickstarter demonstrate that ethical issues often arise when governance fails to keep pace with technological advances. However, increased regulation, stakeholder engagement, transparent algorithms, fair compensation and effective grievance mechanisms can help mitigate these risks. Practical implications The study underscores the need for proactive managerial and policy interventions, including transparent governance mechanisms, fair labour practices, ethical platform design and effective regulatory oversight. Originality/value This study contributes by shifting the focus from general crowdsourcing to professional service contexts, and by integrating ethical theory, legal analysis and case-based evidence to provide a comprehensive, governance-oriented understanding of ethical challenges in digital service ecosystems.

title: Islamic Accounting and ESG Integration for Sustainable Development: A Value-Driven Framework for Ethical Reporting and Sustainability Performance in Shariah- Compliant Firms
summary: ABSTRACT: While sustainability reporting has become a hallmark of corporate accountability in global capital markets, traditional Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) frameworks continue to be largely secular, and they frequently fail to consider the ethical and spiritual aspects that are a part of faith-based accounting frameworks. This study proposes and empirically examines a value-driven conceptual framework that facilitates the relationship between Islamic accounting practices and the quality of ESG disclosure for Shariah-compliant firms and then the link between ESG disclosure quality and sustainable development performance, in which the role of Shariah governance is modeled as a boundary condition moderator. Based on Stakeholder Theory, Maqasid al-Shariah, and Legitimacy Theory, the study proposes that Islamic accounting practices (compliance with AAOIFI standards, disclosure based on Sharia, transparency in the application of Zakat, and ethical reporting) are antecedents of high-quality ESG disclosure (environmental, social, and governance) sub-dimensions, and that high-quality ESG disclosure partially mediates the link between Islamic accounting practices and the sustainable development performance (economic sustainability, social impact, environmental efficiency, and alignment with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)). The model was estimated using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in Software SmartPLS 4 with survey data gathered from finance, accounting, and Shariah-compliance officers in the Shariah-compliant listed firms, supplemented by archival disclosures in listed firms. Robustness checks were conducted in a panel subsample using System Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) technique. The results show that Islamic accounting practices have a significant positive effect on ESG disclosure quality, ESG disclosure quality appears to have a positive effect on sustainable development performance, Islamic accounting practices have both direct and indirect effect on sustainable development performance through the mediation of ESG disclosure quality and Shariah governance significantly enhances the relationship between Islamic accounting practices and ESG disclosure quality. The findings contribute to the literature of ESG by introducing Maqasid al-Shariah as a substantial theoretical framework in sustainability research and are of practical use to standard setters, Islamic financial institutions, Shariah supervisory board, policy makers and socially responsible investors as a replicable, hybrid measurement framework. Regulatory implications for harmonising AAOIFI standards and global ESG taxonomies are addressed, as well as limitations and recommendations for further research. title: ACCESSIBILITY OF ELDERLY CARE SERVICES IN DIGITAL COMMUNITY GOVERNANCE: MECHANISMS, STRUCTURAL BARRIERS, AND INSTITUTIONAL PATHWAYS
summary: The digital transformation of community-based eldercare services has altered the flow of service information and the methods for processing applications. Whether the expansion of digital channels can improve actual service opportunities for older adults depends on the integration of technology with organizational and institutional conditions. This paper employs a comprehensive review of the literature, conceptual analysis, and institutional analysis to define the accessibility of eldercare services as a process-oriented opportunity that spans needs identification, information comprehension, application processing, resource coordination, and service delivery. It constructs an analytical framework in which technology, organization, and institutions jointly shape accessibility. The analysis suggests that information integration, needs identification, resource coordination, support implementation, and feedback-driven course correction constitute the primary mechanisms through which digitalization influences service access. Imbalances between capability requirements and support provision, discrepancies between data categorization and actual needs, disconnects between platform connectivity and accountability, as well as biases in efficiency evaluations, may hinder these mechanisms. New digital barriers may compound economic constraints and supply shortages, while the effectiveness of platform optimization is limited by resource conditions. Governance restructuring aimed at improving accessibility should be guided by actual service access, refining arrangements for channel interoperability, routine assistance, organizational responsiveness, data correction, and equitable evaluation, thereby transforming digital conveniences into inclusive service opportunities.

title: Can organizational image and corporate social responsibility foster citizenship behavior of the employees: a mediational query through organizational identity
summary: Purpose The present research, based upon psychological ownership theory, tries to find out how organizational image and perceived corporate social responsibility (CSR) influence the organizational identity and organizational citizenship behavior (OCB). The present research also tries to find out the role of organisational identity (OI) as a mediator between organizational image and perceived CSR. Design/methodology/approach Survey research using purposive random sampling was conducted in chemical and heavy manufacturing industries in Kolkata, India (N = 243). The survey consisted of a questionnaire measuring the above variables. The data were collected from employees in managerial and supervisory positions. Findings Results were analyzed using SPSS V.25 and Smart-PLS v.4. The mediation model was tested using path analysis. Results show a full mediation effect of organizational identity on the relationship between perceived CSR and OCB and partial mediation of organizational identity on the relationship between organizational image and OCB. Practical implications The results of the present work can have managerial implications. The results of the present research can be used to increase organizational identity and how it can imply a lower attrition rate. Originality/value In today’s scenario, there is an increase in attrition rate especially in emerging economies like India, China and Brazil and there is a need for research to find out what organizational factors are necessary for employees to stay with the organization. The present research tries to find out the psychological mechanism that binds employees to the organization.

title: Mapping E-Readiness Dimensions for Digital Village Development: A Systematic Literature and Bibliometric Review
summary: Digital village development is a key strategy for narrowing the digital gap between rural and urban areas, yet research on e-readiness in this context remains fragmented and predominantly shaped by technical perspectives. This study maps e-readiness dimensions, identifies research trends, and uncovers research gaps in digital villages scholarship. A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) following the PRISMA 2020 framework was conducted on 55 articles published between 2020 and 2026, combining thematic synthesis with an author-keyword co-occurrence bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer. Five principal dimensions of e-readiness were identified: infrastructure and technology, human resources and digital literacy, social and cultural factors, governance and policy, and psychological and individual dimensions. The infrastructure and technology dimension remains the most dominant, reflecting a persistent technical bias not yet matched by attention to social, governance, and psychological readiness factors. Bibliometric analysis shows the research theme continues to be dominated by keywords such as digital transformation, digitalization, digital readiness, and smart village, while social aspects, governance, citizen participation, psychological factors, and rural development outcomes remain relatively underexplored. This research offers a multidimensional mapping of e-readiness for digital village development, framed using a socio-technical readiness perspective as a conceptual synthesis that requires further empirical validation.

title: The Currency of Clarity: Strategic Communication as a Catalyst for Corporate Governance and Market Leadership
summary: Strategic communication connects organizational decisions with the people who must understand, evaluate, implement, or challenge them. This paper examines that connection through a secondary-data analysis and a theory-informed narrative review. It considers how communication may support corporate governance, employee alignment, stakeholder relationships, and the organizational capabilities associated with market leadership. The empirical component uses a traceable Gallup series on global employee engagement and life evaluation for 2015–2024, excluding 2017 because the source does not report a global engagement observation for that year. Contextual evidence comes from Deloitte’s 2024 Gen Z and Millennial Survey and Randstad’s Workmonitor 2023. Descriptive comparisons indicate that global engagement increased from 15% in 2015 to 21% in 2024, with interruptions in 2020 and 2024; these movements do not establish changes in communication quality. The theoretical discussion integrates information asymmetry, the job demands–resources model, and self-determination theory. It develops an explanatory framework in which accurate disclosure, usable information, meaningful feedback, and consistency between messages and conduct may strengthen organizational coordination. The study does not estimate a causal effect on profitability, investor confidence, or market leadership. Its contribution is a reproducible secondary database, a cautious interpretation of year-wise patterns, and a practical framework for communication governance. Limitations include aggregate data, heterogeneous source populations, self-reported measures, and the absence of direct longitudinal communication indicators. The paper concludes that clarity should be treated as a governed organizational capability rather than as a substitute for ethical conduct, adequate resources, or effective management

title: THE MAIN PROBLEMS OF LARGE ENTERPRISES IN UZBEKISTAN: CAUSES, CONSEQUENCES, AND POSSIBLE SOLUTIONS
summary: This article investigates the systemic problems of large, predominantly state-owned enterprises (SOEs) in the Republic of Uzbekistan during its transition to a market economy. Despite their significant share in the country's GDP, large industrial complexes face low profitability, technological backwardness, and severe environmental issues. Based on a literature review and secondary data analysis, the article categorizes the main causes of the efficiency crisis (monopolization, weak corporate governance, outdated infrastructure) and their consequences (threats to energy security, environmental pollution). The concluding section proposes specific mechanisms to address the identified problems, including accelerating privatization programs, implementing ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) standards, and transitioning to International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).

title: Mapping hybrid Infotech competencies for workplace learning: a bibliometric taxonomy and theoretical framework
summary: Purpose This study investigates the growing demand for hybrid information technology (IT) roles that blend technical, strategic, and cognitive skills. It proposes a theoretical Nomological Framework that conceptualizes how multidisciplinary competencies may connect digital transformation with organisational outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A rigorous three-stage analytical procedure was employed, involving data normalization of 114 Scopus-indexed articles, mathematical clustering via VOSviewer to identify thematic patterns, and theoretical synthesis grounded in the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory. Findings The study proposes a taxonomy of hybrid IT competencies and a nomological framework that categorizes multidisciplinary competencies and their development approaches. Four competency domains, Foundational (Red), Strategic (Green), Synergistic (Yellow), and Cognitive (Blue), offer a structured basis for developing future-ready IT professionals in the digital workplace. Research limitations/implications By moving beyond simple skill-listing, the proposed taxonomy provides a theoretical basis for examining competency transitions. It provides a structure for understanding how human capital fosters resilience in volatile digital markets. Practical implications The findings inform the design of evidence-based workplace learning and competency development initiatives. By linking competency domains with appropriate development approaches, the study supports organizations and educators in creating effective upskilling and lifelong learning pathways for the digital workforce. Originality/value The study contributes a bibliometrically derived taxonomy that integrates technical, behavioral, strategic and cognitive competency perspectives within the emerging hybrid IT context.

title: Where ESG enters the investment process: a systematic review of ESG portfolio research
summary: Portfolio outcomes depend not only on asset characteristics but also on how assets are selected, weighted and evaluated. Mixed findings on environmental, social and governance (ESG) portfolios are commonly attributed to differences in data, models, markets, or rating providers, with less attention to the stage at which ESG first enters the investment process. This study addresses that gap through a PRISMA-based systematic review of 201 included studies – 196 research articles and 5 review articles – combined with bibliometric analysis and directed content analysis. A theory-informed, rule-based codebook was applied to the full texts. Each study received one primary role based on the earliest material ESG entry in its principal analytical design. The final coding classified ESG as a Constraint that changes the investable universe in 51 studies (25.4%), a Mechanism that enters portfolio construction or allocation in 77 studies (38.3%), and Evaluation used to assess investment outcomes or behavior in 73 studies (36.3%). The classification distinguishes asset eligibility, portfolio allocation and investment evaluation as separate decision contexts. It provides a structured basis for organizing the literature and interpreting findings with attention to how ESG is used. Its contribution is descriptive and interpretive: the classification does not establish that differences in ESG entry points cause differences in portfolio returns.

title: MANAGEMENT MODEL FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE BASED ON EUROPEAN EXPERIENCE
summary: The article focuses on the development of a management model for the implementation of artificial intelligence technologies in Ukrainian industry, aimed at ensuring a transition from an enterprise’s technological and organizational readiness to measurable performance outcomes from the use of artificial intelligence. The relevance of the study is determined by the need to accelerate the digital transformation of Ukraine’s industrial sector under conditions of limited financial and human resources, energy-related risks, changes in production chains, and the gradual integration of Ukrainian enterprises into the European digital environment. The study systematizes the key prerequisites that determine an enterprise’s capacity to use artificial intelligence technologies, including the state of technological infrastructure, data quality and accessibility, organizational conditions, staff competencies, economic capabilities, and interaction with the external digital environment. The necessity of distinguishing between the concepts of artificial intelligence readiness, artificial intelligence implementation, and artificial intelligence performance is substantiated. The proposed approach provides not only for the possibility of scaling a solution but also for returning to the stage of use-case selection to adjust the selected scenario or terminate the project in cases of insufficient performance. The practical significance of the obtained results lies in the possibility of applying the proposed management logic by managers and specialists of industrial enterprises when developing a portfolio of digital initiatives, selecting artificial intelligence projects, determining criteria for their piloting, and making decisions on scaling. Particular attention is paid to the European experience of using artificial intelligence in industry, particularly in energy, semiconductor manufacturing, automotive manufacturing, and industrial automation, which makes it possible to identify directions for adapting such experience to Ukrainian conditions. The study results in a management model that integrates enterprise readiness, practical technology implementation, assessment of the achieved effect, management decision-making, and subsequent performance into a unified cyclical process.

title: ESG Performance, ESG Controversies, and Stock Volatility in ASEAN-5 Firms
summary: Background: Attention to Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) is increasing in line with the demands of investors and stakeholders for sustainable business practices. However, whether ESG performance and ESG controversies are associated with stock volatility across ASEAN-5 markets remains insufficiently understood. Objective: This study aims to analyze the influence of ESG performance and ESG controversy on company volatility in ASEAN-5 which includes Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and the Philippines during the period 2018–2022. Methods: A five-year (2018–2022) panel of 726 firms from Refinitiv Eikon was analyzed using dynamic-panel System GMM, with descriptive and country-level analyses. Results: The results show that ESG performance has a negative and significant effect on volatility, which indicates that improved ESG performance is related to better stock price stability. Meanwhile, ESG controversy was not significantly associated with aggregate volatility. Analysis by country shows that ESG performance has a significant negative effect in Indonesia, while ESG controversy has a significant positive effect in Thailand. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the influence of ESG performance on volatility has changed, while ESG controversy has not shown a significant influence. Conclusion: These findings suggest that ESG performance can be one of the mechanisms of companies in reducing market risk, while the impact of ESG controversies is still influenced by market characteristics and investor responses in each country. The estimates are associative, and the near-ceiling controversy scores and incomplete estimator diagnostics limit causal interpretation.

title: STRATEGIC MANAGEMENT OF ENTERPRISE RESTRUCTURING BASED ON AN INVESTMENT APPROACH
summary: This article examines the theoretical, methodological, and practical aspects of the strategic management of enterprise restructuring, based on an investment-oriented approach, within the context of economic instability, a transforming competitive environment, and intensifying crisis-related challenges. It is argued that the effectiveness of restructuring initiatives depends not only on the scale of organizational and economic changes but also on an enterprise's capacity to formulate and implement investment strategies aimed at modernizing production potential, optimizing capital structure, enhancing the performance of business processes, and ensuring long-term competitiveness. Strategic restructuring management is defined as a comprehensive process of aligning structural, functional, and investment transformations with the enterprise’s long-term development goals. The economic essence of the strategic management of enterprise restructuring is explored, and the role of an investment-oriented approach in establishing the organizational and economic prerequisites for structural transformation is identified. The key components of the investment support for restructuring are characterized, including the establishment of investment priorities, the mobilization of financial resources, the optimization of funding sources, the assessment of investment risks, and the evaluation of the effectiveness of strategic alternatives. Scientific approaches regarding the interrelationship between investment strategy, the structural transformation of enterprises, and the development of long-term competitive advantages are synthesized. The necessity of integrating investment planning into the strategic management system for restructuring processes is substantiated. The study systematizes the key directions of strategic management in enterprise restructuring, including the modernization of the production and technological base, the reform of the organizational management structure, the optimization of financial and economic processes, digital transformation, the diversification of business activities, and the enhancement of investment attractiveness. Particular attention is paid to developing a mechanism for strategically aligning investment decisions with restructuring priorities; this mechanism entails a comprehensive diagnosis of the enterprise's economic status, the definition of strategic goals, the substantiation of investment alternatives, resource allocation, and the monitoring of the effectiveness of structural transformations. The significance of an investment-oriented approach is established in terms of ensuring enterprise adaptability to changes in the external environment and improving the efficiency with which resource potential is utilized. The study identifies the primary challenges in the strategic management of enterprise restructuring, such as limited investment resources, the high cost of raised capital, economic uncertainty, a lack of alignment between strategic and investment decisions, technological obsolescence in certain production areas, and elevated investment risks. It substantiates the rationale for establishing an integrated organizational-economic mechanism for restructuring management one that combines tools for strategic analysis, investment project design, financial planning, risk management, and the monitoring of transformation process efficiency. Emphasis is placed on the necessity of a differentiated selection of investment instruments, contingent upon the enterprise's financial condition, the severity of its structural imbalances, and its strategic development priorities. It is concluded that applying an investment-based approach to the strategic management of enterprise restructuring creates the prerequisites for ensuring a systematic process of organizational and economic transformation, enhancing the efficiency of capital utilization, strengthening financial stability, and building the potential for long-term development. It is established that the effectiveness of restructuring depends on the alignment of strategic goals, investment opportunities, and the mechanisms used to implement structural changes. The practical significance of these findings lies in their applicability to substantiating investment strategies, developing restructuring programs, and improving strategic management systems within enterprises particularly in the face of crisisrelated challenges and the structural transformation of the economy.

title: Moderating Role of Audit Quality on the Relationship Between Ownership Structure and Firm Value of Listed Nigeria Commercial Banks
summary: This research investigates the impact of audit quality on the relationship between ownership structure and firm performance among listed deposit money banks in Nigeria. Corporate governance remains a critical driver of organizational success, especially in the banking sector, which plays a pivotal role in national economic development. Ownership structure—defined in terms of insider ownership, institutional ownership, and government ownership—has long been recognized as a key factor influencing firm behavior and performance. However, the moderating role of audit quality in this relationship has received limited empirical attention in the Nigerian context. The study adopts a quantitative research design and utilizes secondary data obtained from the financial reports of selected deposit money banks over a period of five years (2021–2025). Descriptive statistics, regression analysis, and ANOVA tests were used to examine the relationships among the variables. Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) was used as the primary indicator of firm performance. Ownership structure variables were treated as the independent (predictor) variables, while audit quality served as a moderating (intervening) variable. The empirical results indicate that ownership structure, particularly insider and institutional ownership, has a significant and positive effect on firm performance. Government ownership, however, exhibited a weaker and less consistent relationship with performance metrics. Audit quality, measured by auditor independence, firm rotation, and compliance with standards, showed a strong and positive moderating effect. High audit quality strengthened the positive impact of insider and institutional ownership on firm performance, suggesting that robust auditing mechanisms can reduce agency problems, increase transparency, and enhance investor confidence. Based on these findings, the study recommends enhancing audit quality standards, promoting continuous auditor training, ensuring auditor independence, encouraging institutional and insider ownership, and strengthening regulatory oversight. These recommendations, if implemented, could lead to improved financial health and governance within Nigeria’s banking sector. This research contributes to the growing literature on corporate governance and audit quality and provides practical insights for bank regulators, investors, policymakers, and academic scholars.

title: Taxing Online Real Estate Businesses in Tanzania: Legal and Regulatory Challenges in the Digital Economy
summary: The digital transformation of Tanzania's real estate sector has significantly changed property advertising, brokerage, rental management, and transactions. Property owners, brokers, and digital intermediaries increasingly rely on websites, online marketplaces, and social media platforms to generate income. While Tanzania has gradually expanded its tax laws and electronic transaction regulations to cover digital economic activities, taxing online real estate businesses remains challenging due to legal and regulatory hurdles. This article critically assesses whether Tanzania’s legal and institutional framework is sufficient for taxing online real estate, highlighting key obstacles to effective tax collection. Using doctrinal legal analysis of relevant legislation, regulations, and literature, alongside comparisons with other jurisdictions and international trends, it shows that the issue is no longer the absence of laws but their fragmented implementation and enforcement. Major challenges include identifying the income earner, defining the roles of property owners, brokers, and platforms, establishing taxable nexus in cross-border deals, obtaining reliable third-party information, and integrating electronic payments and registration data. The article contends that while mandatory electronic payments and stricter taxpayer ID rules improve traceability, they are insufficient without interoperable systems and clearer duties for digital intermediaries. It advocates clearer laws for online real estate agents, stronger third-party reporting, integrated data systems, and technology-driven tax administration. These reforms are essential to enhance compliance, ensure legal certainty, promote fairness, and support sustainable growth of Tanzania’s digital economy.

title: SpectralGuard: a Spectrally grounded λ-SHAP framework for XAI validity certification in pharmaceutical supply chain networks
summary: Permutation-based explainability methods such as SHAP are central to regulatory compliance in AI-governed pharmaceutical supply chains across Sub-Saharan Africa, yet their validity depends on a structural property that existing frameworks do not monitor: the algebraic connectivity of the supply hypergraph, quantified by the Fiedler eigenvalue λ 2 . We prove that λ 2 → 0 is a sufficient condition for permutation-based XAI failure (Theorem 3.5): no increase in sampling effort can recover validity once network connectivity collapses. We introduce SpectralGuard, demonstrated on a calibrated synthetic DGP driven by real Eskom load-shedding and SARB ZAR/USD records ( n = 3, 227 business days, 2014–2026); all spectral results are from the synthetic hypergraph. λ-SHAP shrinks attributions toward a fluid-regime prior using λ 2 ( t ) as the shrinkage weight, maintaining auditability at an explicit bias–variance cost (Remark 3.12). A probabilistic validity certificate V ( t ) combines four spectral metrics with SHA-256 tamper-evidence. An oracle experiment ( B = 500, Seed = 2,026) demonstrates 70.4–89.2% attribution MSE reduction across governance regimes. The spectral gate is the decisive ablation component. In the synthetic DGP, early-warning detection leads classical baselines by 19 business days (λ c alert preceding the λ m crossing). Field validation on real CCMDD procurement data is planned for 2027 (PLMIF-2). A nine-step DHIS2 integration pathway supports SDG 3, 9, 13, and 16.

title: INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NA OTIMIZAÇÃO DO SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT
summary: Este estudo analisou as contribuições da Inteligência Artificial (IA) para a otimização do Supply Chain Management (SCM), considerando suas aplicações, benefícios e desafios em organizações industriais e logísticas. A pesquisa adotou abordagem qualitativa, de natureza bibliográfica, com finalidade exploratória e descritiva. O levantamento concentrou-se em publicações de 2021 a 2026, localizadas na Scientific Electronic Library Online (SciELO), Portal de Periódicos da Coordenação de Aperfeiçoamento de Pessoal de Nível Superior (CAPES), Scopus e Google Acadêmico. A análise foi organizada nas categorias aplicações da IA no SCM, contribuições para a tomada de decisões, benefícios e desafios de adoção. Os resultados indicaram possibilidades de utilização em previsão de demanda, estoques, compras, transporte e planejamento, com contribuições para maior capacidade analítica e antecipação de situações operacionais. Também foram identificados desafios relacionados à qualidade dos dados, integração de sistemas, infraestrutura, investimentos e qualificação profissional. Concluiu-se que a IA contribui para a otimização do SCM quando sua utilização está integrada aos processos e às decisões organizacionais.

title: Agentic AI and Organizational Decision-Making: A Conceptual Framework for Human–AI Collaboration in Digital Transformation
summary: Organizations are now implementing AI technology that goes beyond prediction or recommendation. Agentic systems can pursue a goal, plan steps, call software tools and adapt with little prompting, which unsettles long-standing assumptions about who decides and who answers for the outcome in digital transformation. In this study, a conceptual framework is designed in relation to collaborative work between humans and artificial intelligence in organization decision making in agentic circumstances. With the use of a purposive narrative review of peer reviewed literature and policy documents published from 2019 to 2026, the issue is contextualized within the current global trends, African policy regarding the continent and Kenya’s digital economy. The framework will be designed through the process of iterative synthesis based on three decision attributes (stake, ambiguity, reversibility) and the amount of autonomy assigned to the agent in four types of collaboration; delegate, supervise, co-decide, and reserve. Six testable propositions follow. The paper argues that organizations face a design problem of how to share decisions, not a choice between human and machine decisions, and that in Kenya the design must also respect legal limits on solely automated decisions under section 35 of the Data Protection Act, 2019. Implications for managers and policymakers are outlined, and an agenda for empirical testing is proposed. As a conceptual contribution, the paper reports no new data, and its propositions remain to be tested.

title: De la qualité des systèmes d'information à la performance des processus : une revue critique et un cadre intégrateur fondés sur la théorie des ressources, les capacités dynamiques et la capacité d'absorption
summary: Résumé La littérature sur les systèmes d'information (SI) a largement établi que la qualité d'un système conditionne son succès, mais elle explique moins bien comment cette qualité se transforme, au sein d'une organisation, en meilleurs processus puis en performance. Cet article propose une revue critique et intégrative de ce corpus, mobilisant le modèle de succès des SI de DeLone et McLean, les modèles d'adoption, la théorie des ressources, les capacités dynamiques et la capacité d'absorption. Il montre que les travaux antérieurs convergent sur le rôle de la qualité des SI, mais divergent sur le niveau d'analyse, sur le statut des capacités organisationnelles et sur les conditions humaines de la conversion. Il identifie trois limites majeures : un traitement souvent agrégé de la qualité du SI, une médiation par les capacités rarement spécifiée, et une faible attention aux compétences comme condition d'activation. Sur cette base, l'article propose un cadre conceptuel qui articule la qualité de l'information, du système et du service, une capacité numérique de processus, les compétences numériques, la performance des processus et la performance organisationnelle, ainsi que sept propositions de recherche. Il discute enfin la pertinence de ce cadre pour les entreprises marocaines et propose un agenda empirique. Mots clés : qualité des systèmes d'information ; succès des SI ; DeLone et McLean ; théorie des ressources ; capacités dynamiques ; capacité d'absorption ; transformation digitale ; performance des processus ; Maroc Abstract Research on information systems (IS) has established that system quality shapes IS success, but it explains less well how quality is converted, within organizations, into better processes and then performance. This paper offers a critical and integrative review drawing on the DeLone and McLean model, technology acceptance models, the resource-based view, dynamic capabilities and absorptive capacity. It shows that prior work converges on the role of IS quality but diverges on the level of analysis, the status of organizational capabilities and the human conditions of conversion. The paper proposes an integrative framework linking information, system and service quality, digital process capability, digital skills, process performance and organizational performance, and derives seven research propositions. It discusses the relevance of the framework for Moroccan firms and outlines an empirical agenda. Keywords : information systems quality; IS success; DeLone and McLean; resource-based view; dynamic capabilities; absorptive capacity; digital transformation; process performance; Morocco

title: Artificial Intelligence in Financial Services in India: Adoption, Risks, Regulation and the Future of Fintech Lending
summary: Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping India’s financial services sector, with fintech (digital) lending emerging as a key area of adoption. Built on the country’s large-scale digital public infrastructure, digital lenders increasingly deploy AI across the credit lifecycle. These tools promise to widen formal credit access for new-to-credit and thin-file borrowers, micro and small enterprises, gig workers and low-to-mid-income households. However, they also raise concerns about algorithmic transparency, explainability, discrimination, consumer protection, privacy and cybersecurity. India has no single AI-specific law and oversight instead follows the sector-led, “techno-legal” approach set out in MeitY’s India AI Governance Guidelines (2025), which channels oversight through regulators such as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).This report draws on structured interviews with industry leaders and technology vendors, together with a survey of 21 digital lending firms which are estimated to account for roughly 80% of digital lending volume in the country. The report maps trends in AI adoption, identifies operational and governance challenges, and assesses future trajectories. Firms see productivity gains but cannot yet attribute profitability to AI, which leaves the business case unproven even as investment intentions grow, particularly in collections and customer experience. The most significant risks are data quality, cybersecurity and dependence on third-party vendors. India relies on sector-led, principles-based oversight, and the RBI’s draft model risk guidance is not yet binding, so regulatory ambiguity persists. The central challenge is to extend governance outward to customers, vendors and data supply chains, as quickly as deployment advances.

title: Green Innovation for Sustainable Development in Emerging Economies: The Roles of Organizational Culture, Leadership, and Strategic Capabilities
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines organizational and strategic factors associated with green innovation performance (GIP) in Pakistan's manufacturing sector. Drawing on the resource‐based view (RBV), dynamic capabilities view (DCV), and componential theory of creativity (CTC), it develops an integrated resource‐to‐culture‐to‐performance framework linking green intellectual capital (GIC), environmental consciousness (EC), and green creativity (GCT) with GIP through green organizational culture (GOC), while testing green transformational leadership (GTL) and green competitive advantage (GCA) as boundary conditions. Survey data from 575 managerial respondents were analyzed using PLS‐SEM, complemented by necessary condition analysis (NCA) and importance‐performance map analysis (IPMA). GIC, EC, and GCT were positively associated with GOC, and GOC was positively associated with GIP. The indirect effects through GOC were significant, while all four interaction terms were positive and significant. NCA effect sizes were significant and exceeded 0.10 for all six examined conditions, with bottleneck analysis identifying progressively higher requirements at higher desired GIP levels. IPMA identified GCA as having the highest total‐effect importance, whereas GOC combined relatively high importance with lower performance. The findings provide context‐specific evidence that green resources, awareness, creativity, culture, leadership, and competitive conditions operate as complementary elements of green innovation performance in Pakistan's manufacturing sector.
